items.question: HOW DOES IT WORK?
items.answer: Download the Open Life application or call an adviser on (+237) 681 704 497 to open your account. Once your account has been opened, you will receive a code for checking your account and paying your premiums. You will then be an Open Life customer and can make daily premium payments to prepare your projects with complete peace of mind.

items.question: WHAT DOES THE CONTRACT GUARANTEE?
items.answer: The Open Life contract allows you to build savings day after day for your medium- and long-term projects. All premiums paid earn 2% interest per year. In the event of death or total and permanent disability, capital equal to the total revalued payments will be paid to the designated beneficiary.

items.question: WHEN DOES THE CONTRACT TAKE EFFECT AND HOW LONG DOES IT LAST?
items.answer: The contract takes effect after payment of the first premium. Its effective date is specified in the individual contract conditions. Its duration is selected when the application is signed. The recommended minimum duration is 2 years and the maximum duration is 15 years. The contract is automatically renewed annually when it reaches its expiry date.

items.question: WHEN AND HOW CAN I USE MY SAVINGS BEFORE THE CONTRACT ENDS?
items.answer: From the end of the sixth month of the contract, you can request a partial or full withdrawal of your savings through the application or by using the USSD code. Only a full withdrawal terminates the contract. No withdrawal fees are charged.

items.question: HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO RECEIVE MY SAVINGS?
items.answer: Revalued savings are paid within 48 hours through a direct transfer to your Orange Money or MTN Mobile Money account, according to your preference. The same processing time applies to the payment of the surrender value.

items.question: HOW IS THE CONTRACT FUNDED?
items.answer: The contract is funded by daily payments starting from 200 FCFA. The monthly ceiling is set at 1,000,000 FCFA. You may make additional voluntary payments at any time, including several times during the same day.

items.question: WHAT FEES APPLY TO THE CONTRACT?
items.answer: All charges applied to the contract are zero:

items.title: Article 1: Basis of the contract – Incontestability

content.text: This Open Life contract is governed by the Insurance Code of the Inter-African Conference on Insurance Markets and is subject to the social and tax legislation in force in Cameroon. This legal and tax framework may be amended and may affect the current contract.
The statements made by the policyholder in the insurance application form the basis of the contract, which becomes incontestable as soon as it takes effect.
The insurance exists and takes effect only after the policy has been signed by each contracting party and the first premium has been paid, provided that the insured is alive at the time of payment.
The insurance application and the special conditions form an integral part of this policy.

This Open Life contract is an individual savings contract intended to enable the insured to build up capital to finance projects or supplement retirement income, or to enable a beneficiary to build up capital for entering working life and/or higher education.
The Open Life contract therefore provides for:

items: If the insured is alive at the end of the contract, payment of the capital acquired on the contract end date. At the beneficiary's choice, payment is made either as a lump sum or as an immediate fixed-term annuity.

If the insured dies or becomes totally and permanently disabled before the end of the contract, payment to the designated beneficiary or beneficiaries of the capital acquired at the time of death or disability. This death benefit is settled without any additional payment or special deduction.

content.text: The capital acquired on a given date is equal to the total contributions net of payment charges, increased by profit-sharing allocations and, where applicable, reduced by partial surrenders and outstanding advances.

items.title: Article 4: Effective date – Right of withdrawal

content.text: The contract takes effect after the policy has been signed and the first premium has been paid, provided that the insured person or persons are alive at the time of payment.
The contract automatically ends on the end date stated in the special conditions and upon the death of the insured.

Any policyholder who has signed the policy may withdraw from it by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt, or by any equivalent means providing evidence, within thirty days from the date on which the first premium was paid.
Withdrawal results in reimbursement of the premium paid, less the cost of the policy, within a maximum period of thirty days from receipt of the withdrawal request.
After that period, any unreimbursed amounts automatically bear interest at the statutory rate increased by half for two months, and thereafter at twice the statutory rate.
The company covers all risks of death occurring during the term of the contract, whatever the cause, subject to the following provisions:

items: In the event of foreign war, rebellion, riots, insurrection, civil war or terrorism: in accordance with Article 94 of the Insurance Code, coverage under this policy will take effect only under the conditions determined by the State after hostilities have ended.

If the insured is murdered by the beneficiary: in accordance with Article 78 of the Insurance Code, the insurance contract ceases to have effect in respect of any beneficiary convicted of intentionally causing the death of the insured.

content.text: In accordance with Article 67 of the Insurance Code, the insurer pays the policyholder or the heirs, where the insured was murdered by the beneficiary, an amount equal to the contract's mathematical reserve.

The contract is concluded for a minimum term of eight (8) years. After 10 years, and at the policyholder's written request, the contract may be renewed annually. Renewal may continue until the policyholder's 85th birthday.
Under Article 12 of the Insurance Code, the insured is required, among other things, to:

items: Answer accurately the questions asked by the insurer, particularly in the risk declaration form used when the contract is concluded, regarding circumstances that enable the insurer to assess the risks it is undertaking.

During the contract, disclose any new circumstances that either increase existing risks or create new risks and thereby make the answers previously given to the insurer inaccurate or obsolete. The insured must report these circumstances to the insurer within fifteen days of becoming aware of them. Where a countersigned letter is used, the insured must receive a receipt as evidence.
Notify the insurer, as soon as the insured becomes aware of it, of any claim likely to trigger the insurer's coverage.

Notify the insurer of changes of residence, postal address, landline and/or mobile telephone numbers and, where applicable, email addresses, social-media details, bank details and all geolocation information concerning the insured. The same information, except bank details, must where applicable be provided for beneficiaries, contact persons referred to in Article 8 of the Insurance Code, and the employer. The insurer may not rely on these provisions if it has failed to fulfil its own obligations.

content.text: The premium and related charges, whose amounts are stated in the special conditions of the contract, are payable in advance to the company or to its appointed representative holding written authority.
Premiums may be paid only through mobile payments. Cash payments are not permitted.
The premium amount and due dates are set out in the special conditions.

The insured may make additional payments on each premium due date. The amounts are determined by the insured, subject to a minimum of two hundred (200) CFA francs. However, the total daily premiums collected for each insured, including scheduled and voluntary payments, may not exceed 1,000,000 (one million) CFA francs per month.
The insurer has no right of action to compel payment of premiums relating to Open Life contracts.

Under Article 74 of the Insurance Code, the insurer may not refuse a reduction or surrender once 15% of the premiums or contributions provided for in the contract have been paid, or once at least two (2) annual premiums have been paid.
Under this contract, however, the insured is entitled to surrender savings without restriction from the end of the sixth month of the contract.

Advance: within the limit of the surrender value, the insurer may grant advances to the policyholder. The annual interest rate applicable to the advance must be clearly disclosed to the insured at the time of the transaction.

In accordance with Article 74 of the Insurance Code, this rate may not be lower than the maximum technical rate plus the profit-sharing rate distributed for the latest closed financial year, plus two percentage points. When granting the advance, the insurer must provide the contracting party with an amortisation schedule and an explanatory notice describing how interest and repayments are calculated.
Technical rate (0%) + distributed profit-sharing rate + 2%; the resulting rate may not exceed 7%.
The maximum interest rate is the rate referred to in Article 338(2) of the Insurance Code.

Reduction: at the policyholder's request, or where premiums have not been paid under the conditions of Article 5, the insurer must reduce the insured capital in proportion to the mathematical reserve already accumulated.
Reduction applies once at least two annual premiums or 15% of the premiums or contributions provided for in the contract have been paid, in accordance with Article 74 of the Insurance Code.
The reduced capital remains payable on the same dates and under the same conditions as the initial capital.

No further premiums are payable under a reduced contract, which may be surrendered before its term. The methods for calculating the surrender and reduction values are determined by general regulations that the insurer must make available to the policyholder. The policyholder may request these values at any time.

Surrender: at the policyholder's request, the insurer must pay the total or partial surrender value of the contract within no more than two (2) months. Once the documents required by the contract have been sent to the insurer, it has 15 days from receipt to pay the matured capital. Beyond the regulatory requirements, ACAM Vie will endeavour to pay the capital following a surrender under the conditions set out in Article 14.
Only a total surrender permanently terminates the contract, after which it cannot be reinstated.
The surrender values net of charges for the first eight years are shown in the ‘Surrender Values’ table in the special conditions.

Nullity: under Article 18 of the Insurance Code, independently of ordinary grounds for nullity and subject to Article 80, the insurance contract is void in the event of intentional concealment or misrepresentation by the insured where it changes the subject matter of the risk or diminishes the insurer's assessment of it, even if the omitted or misrepresented risk had no effect on the claim.

Termination: the insured has the right to terminate the contract after six months from the subscription date. Termination requires the insurer to return the contract's mathematical reserve without any penalty.
Forfeiture: this contract contains no forfeiture provision in the event of late premium payments by the insured.
In accordance with Article 28 of the Insurance Code, any action arising from this contract is time-barred two years after the event giving rise to it.
However, this period does not begin:

items: In the event of concealment, omission, or a false or inaccurate statement concerning the risk, until the day on which the insurer becomes aware of it.
In the event of a claim, until the day on which the parties concerned become aware of it, if they prove that they were previously unaware of it.

content.text: Where the insured's action against the insurer arises from a third party's claim, the limitation period begins only on the day that the third party brings legal proceedings against the insured or is compensated by the insured.
The limitation period is extended to ten years for life insurance contracts and for personal accident insurance contracts where the beneficiaries are the legal successors of the deceased insured.

In accordance with Article 7 above, any policyholder who changes their residence or email address must notify the company by registered letter and designate a residence or email address to which all communications may validly be sent.
If no such address is designated, those communications, including registered letters sent to the previous residence or email address known to the insurer, will remain fully effective.

items.title: Article 14: Information provided to the insured

content.text: For as long as your contract requires periodic premium payments, no later than 30 June each year we will provide a contract statement containing the following information as at 31 December of the latest closed financial year:

items: The surrender value.
The reduction value.
The guaranteed capital.
The contract premium.
The minimum guaranteed interest rate for the coming year.

The interest rate corresponding to the amount allocated to the contract's mathematical reserves directly from profit sharing for the previous financial year or from reversals of provisions for surplus participation.

content.text: These amounts may not take account of profit-sharing allocations that have not been definitively awarded.
Each year, the insurer undertakes to submit a proposal for revaluing the capital and insurance premium. The policyholder is free to accept or reject this proposal.
For contracts under which premiums are no longer payable, this information will be provided on request.

Under Articles 81 and 82 of the Insurance Code, insured persons share in the technical and financial profits generated by the company. The minimum total amount to be distributed among all insured persons for a financial year is determined as follows:

items: 90% of the technical profits generated during the financial year across all contracts.
85% of the financial profits.

content.text: The total policyholder profit-sharing amount is distributed in proportion to the mathematical reserve accumulated under each contract.
Insured benefits are paid at the company's registered office after submission of the supporting documents required for settlement, including:

items: A copy of the national identity card.
The insurance contract.

content.text: If the insured dies, the beneficiary or beneficiaries must provide the following documents:

items: A certified copy of the death certificate.
A certified copy of the insured's national identity card.
A certified copy of the identity card of each beneficiary.
A certified copy of the minor child's birth certificate, where necessary.
A life certificate or school attendance certificate for the minor child, where necessary.
A certified copy of the marriage certificate, where necessary.
A completed claim declaration form supplied by ACAM Vie.

content.text: Total, permanent and definitive disability is treated as death and gives entitlement to payment of the death benefit. The insured must provide a medical certificate stating the degree of incapacity and the medical report issued by the insurance company.
Payment of the amounts due is indivisible with respect to the company, which settles against a joint receipt from the interested parties.
The insurer has 24 hours where the beneficiary is the insured, and 48 hours otherwise, from receipt of the documents required under the contract to pay the guaranteed capital.
After the applicable deadlines, unpaid amounts automatically bear interest at the discount rate increased by half for two months and, after that two-month period, at twice the discount rate.

In relations between the insurer, policyholder and insured, errors, omissions or misunderstandings may arise and lead to disputes. In most cases, a timely call to the appropriate ACAM Vie department can resolve the issue quickly. If the response does not satisfy the insured, they may write to:
Open Life – ACAM Vie – Customer Service – PO Box 2000 Douala
or
support.openlife@acamvie.com

As this contract is entered into in good faith, in the event of a dispute you and we agree to abide by the decision of two appointed arbitrators, one chosen by each party. If they disagree, the two arbitrators will appoint a third arbitrator to decide between them. If no agreement can be reached on that appointment, the president of the court of first instance at your place of residence will make the appointment at the request of the most diligent party.

The majority decision of this arbitration panel will be binding on the parties and final. Each party will bear the fees of its own arbitrator, and the parties will share equally the fees of the third arbitrator and the arbitration costs.

faqPage.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqPage.subtitle: Find the answers to your questions

items.question: What is Open Life?
items.answer: Open Life is a secure, fee-free and fully digital daily savings solution based on life insurance, designed to meet the needs of people with low incomes.

items.question: Who can subscribe to Open Life?
items.answer: Anyone who is at least 18 years old and wishes to build savings can subscribe to Open Life.

items.question: Who should I give my money to as part of this savings plan?
items.answer: The savings are transferred directly from the customer to their account through USSD or the Open Life application.

items.question: Does my savings earn interest?
items.answer: Yes. Your savings earn interest at an annual rate of 2%.

items.question: How long does my contract last?
items.answer: The minimum contract duration is one year.

items.question: When can I access my savings?
items.answer: You can access your savings after six full months.

items.question: After six months, how many withdrawals can I make per year?
items.answer: You can make six withdrawals per year, at a rate of one withdrawal every two months.

items.question: Can I subscribe to Open Life by myself?
items.answer: No. You must visit a distributor with your national identity card to open your online savings account.

items.question: What is the minimum amount I can save per day?
items.answer: The minimum premium is 200 FCFA per day.

items.question: What is the maximum amount I can save per day?
items.answer: There is no maximum daily amount.

items.question: Can I make voluntary payments into my account?
items.answer: Yes. You can make voluntary payments as many times as you wish.
